reuse.why: Reuses getDateWithSkippedWeekend, recurConfigToRSchedule and the captureBreadcrumb pattern for the new handler and adds an exported isHoliday, but the daily-skip rule is not given a shared home and each path writes its own weekend-or-holiday check.

duplication.why: The 'weekend or holiday' test appears in three shapes (the loop in getDateWithSkippedWeekend, the find predicate in getNextDate, the condition in getDatesInRange) and the daily-skip rule is decided separately in getNextDate and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: The handler belongs in server/schedules/app.ts, but the daily-skip decision that is a schedule rule is inlined in the handler instead of living in shared/schedules.ts beside the weekend rule.

scope.why: Focused on schedules; the getUpcomingDates edit to pass holidays is in scope, no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: Magic constants (take = 4 in getNextDate, holidays.length + 2 window in getDatesInRange) bound how many consecutive skipped days work, the daily-skip rule exists in two divergent forms, getUpcomingDates does not apply the daily-skip rule at all and schedule-template.ts never passes holidays.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getDatesInRange in server/schedules/app.ts decides the daily weekend/holiday skip itself (config.frequency === 'daily' && (d.isWeekend || isHoliday)) instead of going through a shared schedule rule; getNextDate does the same inline.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily-skip rule is written once as a dates.find predicate with start-bound in getNextDate and again as an if/continue in getDatesInRange; the non-working-day test is reshaped in each of the three places rather than shared.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a skipDailyWeekend special case (with take=4) plus a nested !skipDailyWeekend guard around the helper; getDatesInRange re-implements the daily skip, getUpcomingDates skips the daily rule, and schedule-template.ts calls the helper without holidays.
